tasks.short: Check hours and pay adjustments, then post them in AFAS.

today.trigger: Shift hours, agency hour files and pay adjustments arrive through the week, and they have to be on the payroll record before the monthly run.
steps: Pull roster and attended hours for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo from AFAS and the site sheets.
Match flex hours from the three staffing-agency portals to the order and the person.
Test overtime, night, weekend and allowance lines against the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO.
Chase gaps and clashes with shift leads by Teams or phone.
Post the accepted hours and adjustments onto the AFAS payroll record.
drudgery: Re-keying portal hours into Excel and then into AFAS
Applying the same CAO premium test to hundreds of ordinary lines
Chasing a night-shift or weekend gap the next working morning
today.time_sinks: Matching flex hours to orders, and the back-and-forth on lines that fail a break or premium rule, take most of the 126 hours.

lenses.faster: The line-by-line match and the re-key into AFAS disappear for lines that agree with the roster, the contract and the CAO. The exception queue and the batch sign-off remain, about 30% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A closed shift or an agency hour file starts the match. Lines inside the written rules post themselves onto the payroll record. The specialist releases every held line before it can affect pay.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift crews at Tilburg and Venlo get a same-morning list of rejected hours, while the people who worked are still on site. If that list were cheap, all three sites would want it for every shift pattern, and peak season would add the flex crews, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying portal files into Excel. The work worth keeping is the odd adjustment that changes what someone takes home, where the CAO reading is the real job.
lenses.options: An unclear shift can be priced as overtime, as a compensation hour, or as a warehouse-CAO allowance. The three amounts change which reading the specialist posts, and whether the shift lead accepts it.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from posting lines to tending match rules and clearing the queue. The specialist decides which variance may post and which waits for the site. The job becomes more expert, because the remaining skill is the CAO edge and the routine match has left the desk.
reach: The bookkeeper's match of agency hour invoices to ordered hours, once payroll already holds the accepted hours. Payroll would need each agency's invoice layout and the accounts-payable coding in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: Someone still has to judge hours a roster cannot explain: a supervisor's verbal deal, a safety stop, or a shift that crosses both CAOs. The rules can hold the line; the person who knows the site decides the deal.
tasks.pattern_why: Clock or declared hours, roster, contract and CAO premiums are written rules, so a rules job can match and post them. Free-text adjustments stay in the exception queue for the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: A shift closes, or one of the three agency hour files lands.
steps: Load roster, contract hours, CAO and the hour file for that site.
Post lines that match roster, contract and wage-component rules onto the AFAS payroll record.
Hold lines that miss a name, a break, a premium or an order number.
Show the specialist the held lines with the rule that stopped them.
Write the specialist's decision back to the payroll record and keep the rest out of the run.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases each held line, and releases the batch, before any of it enters the pay run.
data_needed: Employee number, site, CAO, contract hours and scale
Roster start, end and breaks
Declared or clocked start, end and breaks
Agency, order number and flex hours
Wage-component codes for overtime, night, weekend and allowances
Adjustment amount and reason
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS payroll log for the period, with the rule that passed or the person who released each held line.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 posts flex payroll lines automatically once a person has approved the declaration, which is a rule after a human gate.
PayCaptain keeps the pay calculation deterministic and runs repeatable checks around it, including an hourly rate below minimum wage.
A works council must consent before a system processes personnel data, including a new way of reading working time.

risks: A premium rule that is slightly wrong posts the wrong amount to a whole shift before anyone looks.
Agency files arrive late in peak season, or the column layout changes and a clean match is actually shifted.
The works council may treat automatic hour matching as a change to time recording that needs consent.
A check that starts ranking people from time data can become a high-risk system under the EU AI Act from 2 December 2027. This stays a pay match.
research_questions: In the last three pay runs, what share of hour lines posted unchanged, and what share was corrected after someone was paid?
Do the three agency portals export a stable file, or does each month need a hand-built Excel map?
Which CAO premium rules are already AFAS wage components, and which still live only in a specialist spreadsheet?
Would the works council treat this match as a change to the time-registration system that needs consent?

tasks.short: Calculate gross to net in AFAS and enter the wage inputs.

today.trigger: The monthly pay cycle opens, and starters, leavers and one-off corrections arrive around it.
steps: Collect hours, allowances, sick pay, attachments and pension choices for the period.
Type any input that is still missing into AFAS.
Run gross-to-net in AFAS Profit, including wage tax and pension.
Tie the result to last period in Excel.
Correct rejects and send the payment batch toward Rabobank on the current path.
drudgery: Re-typing inputs the hour check already holds
Rebuilding the same Excel tie-out every month
Re-running the whole calculation after one late component
today.time_sinks: The side spreadsheet that re-checks AFAS, and the re-runs after a late leaver or a late allowance, consume most of the 111 hours.

lenses.faster: The parallel Excel gross-to-net and the re-key of inputs that AFAS already holds both disappear. The specialist still reviews the exception list and releases the run, about 40% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Closed hours and an approved employee record for the period start the calculation. AFAS computes gross, deductions, net and the payment file. The specialist releases the run after the held cases are clear.
lenses.ambitious: The controller gets a shadow gross-to-net, on Noordhaven's own CAO scales, set beside each staffing-agency invoice. If that shadow figure were cheap, Finance would use it on every invoice from all three agencies, including peak season, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the monthly tie-out workbook. The work worth keeping is the odd case: an attachment of earnings, a crossed CAO, or a first pay that has to be right for a new warehouse hire.
lenses.options: A CAO scale increase can be paid in this period, next period, or as back-pay. The three journals and nets change whether the controller is willing to release this month's run.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes release, exceptions and wage-component design, with the arithmetic inside AFAS. The specialist decides which component may calculate on its own and which needs a human tick before release. The job is more expert, because the remaining questions are CAO and tax edges.
reach: The accountant's tie-out of the payroll journal to the general ledger. Payroll would need the AFAS ledger mapping and the month-close calendar the controller runs.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist remains the person who releases pay. A wrong wage component pays a whole group the wrong net, and only someone who knows the CAO and the last correction can accept a result the engine has not seen before. The net itself comes from the AFAS rules.
tasks.pattern_why: Gross, wage tax, pension, attachments and CAO components are closed rules, and AFAS already calculates them. A generated net is unacceptable; the specialist releases the rules engine's result.

in_practice.trigger: The hour batch and the employee changes for the period are marked ready.
steps: Feed only released hours and approved employee fields into the AFAS calculation.
Calculate gross-to-net, wage tax, pension and the payment file in AFAS.
Hold anyone whose input is incomplete, whose net swings past the agreed band, or whose component has no rule.
Clear the holds, then calculate again.
Release the run and send the payment batch toward Rabobank on the existing approval path.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases the run. No payment file leaves AFAS before that release, and any employee can ask for a person to review their result.
data_needed: Released hours and wage components for the period
Tax credit choice, pension scheme and attachments
CAO, scale, step and part-time factor
Cost center and site
Bank account and payment blocks
Last period's gross and net for the same person
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS pay-run id, the calculation log and the released payment-batch reference.

evidence.claim: Workday states that a probabilistic guess is not good enough in payroll and finance, because almost right means someone is paid incorrectly.
PayCaptain says its AI does not touch how pay is calculated, which stays deterministic, rules-based and repeatable.
AFAS Profit 8 keeps wage-component history and job schemes, and it can approve payroll lines by rule after a person approves the declaration.
A rule-based pay decision still needs a route to a human review.

risks: One bad component replicates across everyone on that CAO in a single run.
A second calculator for the flex shadow figure will drift unless it uses the same AFAS rules as employee pay.
The Rabobank payment file still needs the current approval path; a faster run must not skip it.
Visma has promised payroll AI on Nmbrs and has not shipped it, so waiting for a suite agent leaves the run on today's manual tie-out.
research_questions: How many wage-component amounts does the specialist still type per run, and which of those already exist elsewhere in AFAS?
How many corrections does a typical run produce after release, and which component causes them?
Can AFAS price a flex worker on the in-house CAO scale without creating an employee record that pollutes headcount?
What sample of agency invoices does the controller check today, and would they use a full shadow gross-to-net?

tasks.short: Keep holiday, ADV and sick balances right in AFAS.

today.trigger: Holiday requests, sick calls and returns arrive through the week, and balances have to be right before the pay run because they change the wage.
steps: Register approved holiday, ADV and personal leave against the roster.
Record sick reports from the sites, including partial days and night shifts.
Update balances for the part-time factor and the accrual rules in both CAOs.
Watch long sick spells against the Wet verbetering poortwachter dates that change sick pay.
Answer managers and employees who disagree with a balance.
drudgery: Retyping a sick call that arrived as a Teams message
Fixing a balance after a shift was entered as holiday
Rebuilding part-time accrual in Excel when AFAS and the sheet disagree
today.time_sinks: Reconstructing what a night shift actually took, and sick-pay percentages that change with the length of absence, take most of the 110 hours.

lenses.faster: Retyping a clear Teams or mail message into AFAS disappears. Disputes, partial return to work and the poortwachter file remain, about half of today's time, including the review of every sick entry.
lenses.autonomous: An approved holiday request, or a site message that names a person, a date and a type, starts it. A manager-approved holiday updates the AFAS balance on its own. Any sick entry, any cut in sick pay and any move in a poortwachter date waits for the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Each HR business partner gets a warning two weeks before a sick-pay step or a Wet verbetering poortwachter date changes the wage. If that warning were cheap, the three sites would want it on every long-term case, and they would ask for the week-6 and week-42 dates as well, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping sick calls. The work worth keeping is the disputed balance and the judgment on partial return to work, with the HR business partner.
lenses.options: A disputed day can be paid as sick, as holiday, or unpaid. The three drafts change the net, the remaining balance and which outcome the employee and the manager will accept.
lenses.altitude: Ordinary holiday posting leaves the desk, and the week is balance exceptions and sick-pay judgment. The specialist can hold a sick-pay step until the HR business partner has seen it. The work is more expert on poortwachter pay rules.
reach: The HR administrator's recording of site leave and sick messages into AFAS. Payroll would need the absence types the administrator uses and the shift-lead contacts per site.

tasks.human_edge: Partial return, a disputed sick day and the moment sick pay changes are judgments about a person's situation. The specialist, with the HR business partner, owns those calls. A draft entry can propose the dates; it cannot decide that someone is fit and back.
tasks.pattern_why: The hard input is a Teams note, a mail or a half-filled form. One model call turns that into person, dates and type for AFAS, which then applies the accrual rules. The medical sentence stays out of the call.

in_practice.trigger: A manager approves a leave request in AFAS, or a shift lead sends a sick or return message.
steps: Read only the person, the dates and the label the sender already used, such as holiday, sick or partial return.
Draft the AFAS absence entry and the balance it would produce.
Let AFAS apply CAO accrual and the sick-pay percentage from the dates.
Flag any entry that changes sick pay or a poortwachter date and send that flag to the HR business partner as well.
Post the entry only after the required person confirms it.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist confirms every sick entry and every sick-pay change before it hits the pay run. Manager-approved holiday can post on the manager's approval.
data_needed: Employee number, site, CAO, part-time factor and leave year
Current holiday, ADV and sick balances
Absence type, start, end and partial-return hours
Sick-pay percentage steps in the applicable CAO
Poortwachter dates already on the file
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS absence log, naming who confirmed the entry and which message it came from, with the medical text left in the original mail.

evidence.claim: Once a person approves a declaration, AFAS Profit 8 can approve the related payroll lines by rule, which is the right shape for an approved leave entry flowing into pay.
Works council consent is required for a system that processes personnel data. Sick leave is part of that data.
In a 2026 PayrollOrg survey, more than 46% of US respondents were uncomfortable with AI in payroll, and in 2024 53% objected to AI answering payroll questions.
A change in sick pay is a decision with legal effect and needs a route to a human review.

risks: Sick reports are health data. Sending the medical sentence to an external model can breach the AVG, even when the dates would have been useful.
A wrong sick-pay step underpays someone who is already ill.
A vague night-shift message produces a confident wrong draft, and warehouse staff who never open AFAS still depend on the shift lead.
The payroll entry is a pay fact. The reintegration file under the Wet verbetering poortwachter stays with the HR business partner.
research_questions: What share of absence entries start as Teams or mail, by site and by shift, and what share already start in AFAS?
Will the privacy officer allow a model to read those messages if the medical sentence is stripped and the call stays in the EU under Noordhaven's contract?
Does the works council's existing AFAS consent cover this intake, or is it a new consent under WOR article 27?
How often did a sick-pay percentage change during a run because a poortwachter date was missed?

tasks.short: Update payroll for starters, transfers, tax choices and leavers.

today.trigger: HR administration records a hire, a move between sites, a change to the payroll tax credit, or a resignation.
steps: Read the contract, the transfer mail or the resignation.
Enter scale, hours, cost center, tax credit and end date in AFAS payroll.
Set the recurring components: travel, shift pattern and pension.
For a leaver, flag unused leave and the final period.
Keep a side list of changes that must wait for the next run.
drudgery: Copying fields that are already on the approved contract
Chasing a missing citizen service number or tax-credit form
Maintaining a personal Excel list of changes to apply next month
today.time_sinks: Leavers with open leave, and transfers that change site or CAO, take most of the 95 hours, because each one is a small file.

lenses.faster: When the approved HR record is complete, copying it into payroll fields disappears. Incomplete files and leavers remain, about 45% of today's time, including the check of every cross-CAO move.
lenses.autonomous: An approved hire, transfer, tax-credit change or resignation on the AFAS employee record starts the map. Standard fields write themselves onto the payroll record. The specialist handles incomplete files, cross-CAO transfers and leavers.
lenses.ambitious: Seasonal flex workers who convert to employment get a payroll record in the conversion week, a group whose pay data today sits at the agency until someone retypes it. If that conversion were cheap, recruitment would convert people during the peak, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing a scale and a cost center that are already on the contract. The work worth keeping is the leaver who disagrees about unused leave, and the transfer that changes which CAO applies.
lenses.options: A move from the Tilburg warehouse CAO to the Rotterdam transport CAO can be paid on either scale for the transition month. The two nets change whether the manager and the employee accept the move date.
lenses.altitude: Routine master data flows from the approved contract, and the week is exceptions and leaver files. The specialist can keep an incomplete change out of the run. The job is more expert on settlement and on moves between the two CAOs.
reach: The compensation and benefits specialist's loading of an already agreed scale onto an employee who transfers. Payroll would need the AFAS job-scheme table, and which changes Compensation and Benefits still has to clear with the works council.

tasks.human_edge: The payroll consequence of a disputed resignation, a transition payment, or a move between the two CAOs has to match the agreement the manager actually made. The specialist is the person who can see that the form and the deal differ.
tasks.pattern_why: Once HR has approved the contract or the change, scale, hours, site, tax credit and end date follow by a written map. A resignation that exists only as a letter is returned to the starter-paperwork path for a checked draft.

in_practice.trigger: HR administration sets an AFAS contract, transfer, tax-credit choice or end date to approved.
steps: Read the approved fields and the current payroll record.
Write scale, hours, cost center, CAO, pension and tax credit onto the payroll record when the map is complete.
Hold cross-CAO transfers, leavers with unused leave, and any record with a missing citizen service number, bank account or tax choice.
Price the transition month on both scales when a transfer crosses CAOs, and show both to the specialist.
Apply the specialist's choice and drop the side list for anything the map already carried.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases cross-CAO transfers, leaver settlements and any record the map held. Same-CAO changes with a complete approved file pass on HR administration's approval.
data_needed: Approved contract: CAO, scale, step, hours, site, cost center, start or end date
Payroll tax credit choice and citizen service number status
Pension scheme and recurring allowances
Unused leave balance for a leaver
Open attachment or loan that must stop on the end date
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS employee-dossier audit, with the approved HR event id and the person who released any hold.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes for pay transparency and keeps wage-component history, so a transfer can update a scheme from the approved record.
A leaver settlement or a tax-credit change is a decision with legal effect and needs a route to a human review.
Two CAOs and seasonal flex conversion multiply the variants, so the map has to stay explicit.

risks: An end date one period early stops a wage.
A payroll tax credit applied from a bad or missing form creates a tax debt for the employee.
Recruitee offer data can be staler than the signed contract. The signed AFAS contract has to be the source.
A flex conversion copies agency data into an employee file, which needs a purpose the person was told about.
research_questions: When payroll hears of a change, which fields are already filled on the AFAS contract, and which arrive only as mail?
How many starters and flex conversions in the last year missed the first run or were paid by a manual correction?
How many transfers a year cross the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO?
Is the side Excel still the list of record for next-month changes, or does an AFAS workflow already exist?

tasks.short: Find and clear pay discrepancies before the run is released.

today.trigger: The draft pay run is ready, or a manager calls because a payslip looks wrong.
steps: Compare this period's gross, hours and components with last period and the contract.
Scan for a large swing, a pension line that stopped, a leaver paid twice, or a rate under the CAO minimum.
Open AFAS, the roster and the agency file to see which source is wrong.
Correct the source and recalculate that person.
Note the cause so the same error is recognizable next month.
drudgery: Building the comparison spreadsheet by hand
Scanning pages of output for one bad line
Writing the same explanation to a manager from memory
today.time_sinks: The hunt takes the time. Most of the 95 hours go to finding which of about 1,200 payslips moved for a bad reason.

lenses.faster: The search and the month-on-month spreadsheet disappear. Each flag arrives with the figures that tripped it and a draft reason. Deciding and correcting remain, about 35% of today's time, including reading every flag.
lenses.autonomous: The draft run starts the checks. Written rules flag a gross swing, a stopped pension, a leaver paid two nets and a rate under the CAO minimum. One model call drafts the reason, and the specialist accepts or corrects each flag before release.
lenses.ambitious: The same checks run after each weekly hour post, so a bad adjustment can be refused in the week it is entered. If that were cheap, managers would send more mid-month corrections, because the decision to accept them would be available every week, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss building the comparison sheet. The work worth keeping is the flag that is a real CAO question, or a manager who deliberately overrode the roster.
lenses.options: A gross swing can be explained as a true overtime peak, a duplicate line, or a late allowance. The three reconciliations, with the net of each, change whether the specialist corrects the run or lets the figure stand.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a short queue and a tighter release. The specialist can block the run on a flag and can retire a check that cries wolf. Designing the threshold is the expert work; scanning pages leaves.
reach: The controller's plausibility review of the payroll journal, limited to a wage total that moved without a headcount or CAO reason. Payroll would need the materiality level the controller already uses.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a large swing is a real peak at Venlo, and a fair pay, is the specialist's call. The check can prepare the figures and a sentence; the person who knows the site's week accepts the cause and clears the flag.
tasks.pattern_why: The discrepancies are found by written checks. One model call then drafts the reason from those figures, inside a fixed queue, and the specialist approves the reason before the run moves. The money stays on the AFAS result.

in_practice.trigger: A draft AFAS run is calculated, or a weekly hour batch is posted.
steps: Run the written checks: gross swing, pension stopped while enrolled, leaver with two nets, hourly rate under the CAO minimum.
Attach the component, the two amounts, the threshold and the source record to each flag.
Ask the model for a short reason that cites only those attached figures.
Specialist marks each flag as correct and clear, or sends it back to the source to be fixed.
Recalculate the people who were fixed, then allow release only when the queue is clear.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each flag before the run can be released. A drafted sentence never clears a flag on its own.
data_needed: Draft gross, net and wage components per person
Prior period gross, net and components
Pension enrolment and the pension line
Leaver flag and number of nets in the period
CAO minimum hourly rate, paid hours and gross
The source document id for hours or the adjustment
in_practice.logs_to: The pay-run exception log in the SharePoint month folder, next to the AFAS run id, with the rule, the drafted reason and the specialist's decision.

evidence.claim: In production, PayCaptain checks whether gross moved more than expected, whether pension contributions stopped for someone still enrolled, whether a leaver was paid double net, and whether an hourly rate is below minimum wage. The calculation stays untouched.
Workday's announced Payroll Agent is described as flagging items outside defined parameters and drafting employee notices for payroll to check. Early adopters are set for early 2027.
A dashboard that scores people from time data can be high-risk under the EU AI Act from 2 December 2027. A back-office pay check is the narrower case.

risks: A threshold set too wide misses a real underpayment. Set too narrow, the queue is ignored and the check becomes noise.
A fluent reason can cite the wrong cause. The specialist who trusts the sentence will clear a bad pay.
No Dutch employer in the sources has published error rates, so the bands have to be tuned on Noordhaven's own runs.
Using the same hour data to rank warehouse productivity would cross into a different, higher-risk purpose and needs works council consent.
research_questions: Of the corrections in the last six runs, how many match the four check shapes, and how many had another cause?
What swing size would have caught those corrections and still left a queue one person can clear in a morning?
Are CAO minima and pension enrolment already AFAS fields the check can read?
Does a drafted sentence clear the queue faster than the figures alone, measured on one real run?

tasks.short: Fill in arrival and departure times on the time sheets.

today.trigger: A shift or a week closes with arrival or departure still blank for people who did not record a time.
steps: Collect rosters and the paper or Excel charts from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Fill blank arrival and departure from the roster or from a shift lead's note.
Check breaks and times that cross midnight on the night shift.
Send the sheet back when a name or a time is missing.
Hand the finished times to the hour check.
drudgery: Typing times the roster already implies
Reading photographed paper charts from a weekend shift
Chasing one missing departure several days later
today.time_sinks: Blanks and paper charts from night and weekend shifts, which arrive late and incomplete, use most of the 84 hours.

lenses.faster: Typing a standard shift that matches the roster disappears. A supervisor still confirms every time the roster did not predict, which is about 55% of today's effort once review is counted.
lenses.autonomous: A closed shift with a roster and a chart or note starts it. One model call proposes arrival, departure and break. The shift supervisor approves any time the roster did not predict before payroll can use the sheet.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers' arrival and departure, which today sit only in the agency portal, become a sheet the bookkeeper can read before the invoice is paid. If that were cheap, all three agencies would be asked for it in peak season, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing standard shift times. The work worth keeping is the short call with a shift lead about a crew that stayed for a breakdown.
lenses.options: A night shift that overruns can close at the planned time with overtime on a separate line, or close at the real departure. The two sheets change the premium and the rest gap, so the supervisor's choice changes the pay.
lenses.altitude: Payroll stops completing ordinary sheets. The week keeps the sheets a supervisor could not close, and the specialist can send a sheet back until the site confirms it. Less typing, more judgment on the leftover cases, so the expert part of the job grows while this task shrinks.
reach: The HR administrator's weekly chase of incomplete site attendance. Payroll would need the administrator's contact list per site and the roster fields the sheet is filled from.

tasks.human_edge: Only someone at the site knows whether a person was there when the roster, the badge and the paper disagree. The specialist must leave a blank as a blank. Inventing a departure to close the run is the failure mode.
tasks.pattern_why: Paper charts, photos and short Teams notes are messy. One model call proposes arrival, departure and break as fields the supervisor can accept or correct. A roster match for an ordinary shift can sit beside it as ordinary software.

in_practice.trigger: A shift ends and the roster is available, with or without a chart or a shift-lead note.
steps: Propose the roster's arrival, departure and break for each planned person.
Where a chart or note is attached, one model call proposes the times it actually states, including a midnight cross.
Leave any person the source does not mention as blank.
Send blanks and clashes to the shift supervisor to confirm or correct.
Pass only confirmed times into the hour match.
in_practice.human_gate: The shift supervisor confirms every time that differs from the roster, and every flex time, before payroll can post it.
data_needed: Roster person, site, shift start, shift end and break
Any clock stamp already stored
The chart image or the shift-lead note
Contracted hours and night-shift flag
Agency and order number for flex names on the crew
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS time record, with the source of the proposed time and the supervisor who confirmed it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 already supports a human approval followed by automatic payroll lines, which is the shape of a supervisor confirming a time and the lines following.
Works council consent is required for a system that processes personnel data, including working-time records.
Annex III of the EU AI Act covers worker-scoring uses of time data; the high-risk date cited for that path is 2 December 2027. Completing a sheet for pay is a narrower purpose.
A messy timesheet is the sort of document one model call can turn into fields inside a fixed workflow. Whether Noordhaven's sheets are still messy is untested.

risks: A proposal that fills a blank with the roster time hides absence and overpays, or hides overtime and underpays.
Photos from a warehouse are poor input. A confident wrong time is worse than a blank.
The works council is likely to treat this as a change to working-time records and to require consent.
If the filled times are later used to score output per person, the purpose moves toward a high-risk system from 2 December 2027.
research_questions: Where do arrival and departure live today for each site: AFAS, a clock export, Excel, or paper, and what share is blank when payroll sees it?
On a sample of four weeks, how often does the true time differ from the roster?
Will shift supervisors, including on nights, confirm a prefilled sheet before the crew leaves?
Will the works council consent to a tool that reads shift charts and proposes times?

tasks.short: Put new-hire paperwork into the payroll system.

today.trigger: A signed contract arrives from HR administration, or an offer is marked accepted in Recruitee, often close to the start date.
steps: Collect the contract, the tax-credit form, bank details, site, scale and hours.
Check the pack is complete enough to pay someone.
Enter the employee and the wage components in AFAS.
Set the first period, the cost center and the CAO.
Park an incomplete file so the person is not paid on a guess.
drudgery: Re-typing the contract into AFAS
Chasing a missing tax-credit form by mail
Copying the same starter onto a personal checklist
today.time_sinks: Incomplete files, and people who start before the papers arrive, use most of the 79 hours. The chase takes longer than the typing.

lenses.faster: Typing from a complete typed contract into AFAS disappears. The missing-document chase and a check of scale, CAO and first period remain, about half of today's time, because every starter is still reviewed.
lenses.autonomous: A contract marked signed, or an offer marked accepted, starts a draft payroll record. The draft waits. The specialist confirms identity, tax credit, scale and CAO before the person can be paid.
lenses.ambitious: The recruiter and the new warehouse hire get a first-pay note before day one: first pay date, scale, and the documents still missing. If that note were cheap, recruitment would want it for every peak-season wave and every Friday start, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss re-typing a contract. The work worth keeping is the judgment that a file is safe to pay, and the first-week question from a new hire who does not yet trust the company.
lenses.options: A late file can start in the current period, with a manual payment, or in the next period on the normal run. The two drafts change the first net, the holiday accrual and whether the HR business partner holds the start date.
lenses.altitude: The week is incomplete files and first-pay exceptions. The specialist can keep a starter out of the run until the file is safe, and can tell the recruiter what a late contract does to the first pay. The job is more expert on whether this person can be paid.
reach: The HR administrator's assembly of the payroll slice of the starter packet. Payroll would need the administrator's document list and the Recruitee stage that means the offer is accepted.

tasks.human_edge: Checking that the person, the citizen service number, the bank account and the signed scale belong together is the specialist's release of the first pay. A wrong match pays the wrong person or sets every later period on the wrong scale.
tasks.pattern_why: The contract and the tax-credit form are documents with a fixed target, the AFAS starter fields. One model call drafts those fields for approval. Citizen service number, bank account and identity copies stay out of the model and are checked by the specialist. The later gross-to-net stays in AFAS.

in_practice.trigger: Recruitee shows the offer accepted, or the signed contract is stored on the employee file.
steps: Read the contract for CAO, scale, step, hours, site, cost center and start date.
Draft the AFAS payroll fields from those clauses and list anything missing.
Leave citizen service number, bank account and identity documents for the specialist to enter from the source.
Show two first-period options when the start date falls after the run cut-off.
Create the payable record only after the specialist confirms the draft.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist confirms every new payroll record before the first run can pay it.
data_needed: Signed contract clauses: CAO, scale, step, hours, site, start date
Payroll tax credit form status
Bank account and citizen service number, held outside the model call
Recruitee offer stage and recruiter name
Pay-cycle cut-off and the next two pay dates
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier audit and the starter checklist in the SharePoint pay-run folder, with the contract version the draft was taken from.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit is the payroll record, and its flex pattern already waits for a person to approve before lines post. A starter record needs that same gate.
A bot or tool that reads the personnel file needs works council consent under WOR article 27.

Article 50 of the EU AI Act requires that a chatbot identify itself as AI. Combined with PayrollOrg's finding that 53% of 2024 respondents objected to AI answering payroll questions, the first-pay note stays the specialist's message.
The first pay decision needs a route to a human review.

risks: Passport scans, the citizen service number and bank details are high-risk data. A general model should never receive them.
A drafted scale that looks plausible, and is wrong, sets every later run.
Recruitee can disagree with the signed SharePoint contract. The signed contract wins.
The works council and the processing record have to be in place before a tool reads starter files. A wrong first pay also hits week-one onboarding, which the company tracks.
research_questions: Which starter fields are already structured in Recruitee or AFAS when the offer is accepted, and which exist only on the signed PDF?
How many new hires in the last year were paid late or by a manual payment, and which document was missing?
Will the privacy officer permit a model to read the contract if the citizen service number, bank account and identity copy are excluded?
Does the works council treat this as a change to the personnel system under WOR article 27?

tasks.short: Compile hours, output and pay data for the run and the reports.

today.trigger: Pay-cycle close, and the later requests from Finance and HR for the same numbers.
steps: Pull hours, absence, wage components and headcount from AFAS.
Add flex hours and invoice totals from the three agency portals.
Add warehouse production figures where a report or a premium needs them.
Tie the totals to last period and to the draft journal in Excel.
Send the pack to the controller and answer the questions when Power BI looks different.
drudgery: Refreshing the same extracts into the same workbook
Repairing a VLOOKUP when an agency file arrives with a new layout
Explaining a difference that is only a timing gap between AFAS and the nightly Power BI refresh
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the workbook, and tying flex totals to invoices, use most of the 78 hours.

lenses.faster: The workbook rebuild disappears. A fixed extract ties hours, pay and flex totals and lists only the rows that break. Those rows, and a short read before the pack goes to Finance, are about 30% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The draft run and the arrival of the three agency files start the tie-out. Clean totals compile on their own. The specialist accepts the pack, including every break, before Finance closes on it.
lenses.ambitious: The works council and the HR director get a gender-pay pack by CAO job scheme and site, refreshed when wage components change, well before the first report over 2027 pay. If a refresh were cheap, they would want it after each CAO increase and each peak-season hiring wave, because a gap of 5% or more starts a joint evaluation, so demand would grow past the yearly duty.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the spreadsheet. The work worth keeping is explaining a break that changes a site's cost, in the conversation with Finance.
lenses.options: A border-line set of hours can be compiled as own overtime or as agency cost. The two packs change whether the controller accrues the invoice this month.
lenses.altitude: Assembly leaves the week. What stays is the breaks and the conversation with Finance, and the specialist certifies the pack the controller and FP&A use. The job is more expert about what the figures mean.
reach: The FP&A analyst's monthly collection of payroll actuals by site. Payroll would need the cost-center tree and which flex costs FP&A treat as external hires.

tasks.human_edge: Certifying that a break is understood, before Finance relies on it, stays with the specialist. A tie-out can show a difference. When the agency file and the roster are each internally consistent, a person decides which source is the truth.
tasks.pattern_why: Compiling and tying known extracts is a join and a set of equalities, down to the cent. Ordinary software can do that. The gender-pay figures are the same wage components, grouped by the job scheme AFAS already stores.

in_practice.trigger: The draft AFAS run is released to review, and the three agency hour or invoice files have arrived.
steps: Join hours, absence, gross, employer cost and headcount by person, site and CAO.
Tie flex hours to the agency file and list every difference over the agreed tolerance.
Build the gender-pay inputs from the AFAS job scheme: pay by scheme, site and sex, with the count behind each average.
Hold any total that misses last period's bridge or the draft journal.
Store the pack once the specialist certifies it, for the controller, FP&A and the nightly Power BI extract to use.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist certifies the pack, breaks included, before Finance or the works council uses it. Production figures stay out of any individual score.
data_needed: AFAS hours, absence, wage components, gross, employer cost and headcount
Job scheme, CAO, site, sex and hours fraction for the pay-gap grouping
Agency name, order, hours and invoice amount
Cost center and the journal draft
Last period's certified totals for the bridge
in_practice.logs_to: The certified pack in the SharePoint month-close folder, with the AFAS run id and the journal number it ties to.

evidence.claim: PayCaptain treats the figures around payroll as deterministic and repeatable, with the calculation left on the rules engine.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes for pay transparency and shows wage-component history, which is the grouping a pay-gap pack needs.

Under the bill in the Tweede Kamer, an employer of 1,200 people reports the gender pay gap yearly. The first report covers 2027 pay and is due 7 June 2028. A gap of 5% or more, still unexplained after six months, triggers a joint evaluation with the works council. The council also consents to the job-evaluation system. The bill's fine is up to €11,000, and the start date is by royal decree.
Joining extracts and testing that totals match is rules work. A model adds nothing to a cent-level tie-out.

risks: A second pack that does not match AFAS will be used by mistake once FP&A starts to trust the feed.
An agency file whose columns have shifted can tie cleanly to the wrong hours.
Joining warehouse production to pay, at person level, can slide into scoring workers. That needs works council consent and, from 2 December 2027, may be high-risk.
The certified pack will be treated as official. A quiet error becomes the FP&A actual and, later, the pay-gap report. The legal dates can still move, because the bill starts by royal decree.
research_questions: How many hours a month does the workbook take, and which tabs are pure extracts from AFAS?
Have the three agency exports kept a stable layout over the last six months?
Do AFAS job schemes already hold sex, scheme and site in a way that can produce the averages the bill describes?
Who would stop keeping their own sheet if this pack were certified weekly, and which decision would actually change?

role.altitude: The specialist becomes the person who sets the pay checks, releases a run that is right the first time, and explains the odd result to managers, Finance and the works council. The week is exceptions, CAO changes and the quality of the run. Decision rights grow with that: block a run, refuse an incomplete starter, and decide which variances may post on their own. The job is more expert.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable): match the three agencies' hour invoices to hours payroll has already accepted, and code the invoice in AFAS.
Accountant: tie the released payroll journal to the general ledger and prepare the figures behind the wage-tax filing.
HR administrator: complete the payroll fields on starter, transfer and leaver files once the contract is approved.
Controller: do the first plausibility pass on the wage total, up to a materiality the controller still sets.
Compensation and benefits specialist: load an agreed CAO scale into AFAS wage components. Policy and the works council conversation stay with Compensation and Benefits.
People analytics and HRIS analyst: publish first-time-right and corrections per run from the pay-run log onto the existing Power BI extract.
FP&A analyst: take the certified payroll actuals by site, including own staff versus flex, as the monthly source.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 780 hours a year and just under half the role. The rest, including employee questions, the wage-tax filing, audits and the Rabobank batch, stays on the same person. Month-end cannot also hold a CAO rewrite. Two CAOs, three agencies and works council consent limit how many new feeds one specialist can stand behind. Peak season, when flex headcount moves from about 150 to about 300, is the real ceiling, because the exception load grows while the release of pay remains a human act.
skills_to_grow: Writing AFAS wage-component and check rules so they can be tested on last month's run before they go live
Reading both CAOs well enough to price a transfer, a flex shadow wage and a sick-pay step
Enough of the general ledger and agency-invoice coding to certify the pack Finance uses
Privacy and works council practice for any new use of personnel data or sick data
The pay-transparency figures in the bill: own pay, the average for equal work, and the gender pay gap by job scheme
role.ambitious_version: The specialist runs pay so that a new warehouse hire and a night-shift worker see a correct first wage, a flex invoice is priced against the CAO before it is paid, and the works council sees the gender pay gap building after each CAO change, in time to act before the report over 2027 pay. Corrections per run become rare. The month is then about CAO change and the cases the rules cannot hold. If the checks stay cheap, FP&A, the sites and the recruiters will ask for them more often, and this seat becomes the person Finance and the works council call when a wage figure will be used for a decision.
